title: RWB-S6-E6006: the agreement-and-notices step carries an empty C row although it consumes rwb-document, rwb-comms, rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-decision, and five consumed operations have no published name
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; Work Package B2-S6-009 story lines RWB-S6-E6006-APP and RWB-S6-E6006-CON (H, C, I, X); FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.10.2 and A2.10.3.1; TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T2, T3.1, T4, T5.1, T5.2, T6.1 and Appendix T-A; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 41 and 43; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DS-23; legacy RWB-E6-006
section: Metadata (Contract dependencies, Integration dependencies, External dependencies); Sections 3, 4, 12.2, 12.8, 13 and 18
description: (1) The plan gives H = RWB-S6-E6006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON and C, I and X = None, while the step cannot run without the agreement of P5 rwb-document, the notices of P6 rwb-comms, the customer fact of P1 rwb-source-data, the case state and move answer of P3 rwb-case and the package in force of P7 rwb-decision: six consumed rows and five class C dependencies the metadata does not carry. (2) No source publishes an operation name for the document generation, the notice issue, the customer fact read, the case-move answer or the rule-package read, so all five carry the placeholder. (3) The document run adds a Temporal dependency on the rwb-document queue that no H, C or I row expresses. (4) The legacy Data table lists recovery_case, v_ace_customer, notice, decision_log_entry and rule_row as if they were the step's own data, and all five are other owners' in the target.
evidence: Work Package B2-S6-009 story line RWB-S6-E6006-APP with H of three CON stories and empty C, I, X; FSD S6 A2.10.2 'Integration points. Workbench, WIN' and A2.10.3.1 VR-S6-010-1 and BR-S6-010; TSD S6 T5.2 'Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices'; Architecture v5 slide 19 S6 OUT (Temporal DebtSaleWorkflow, Decision: child: approval, Document: data room pack) and slide 41 rows P5 and P6; legacy RWB-E6-006 Data table rows recovery_case, v_ace_customer, notice, decision_log_entry and rule_row
proposed: Build against the plan's H row and the published documents and fakes of the five owners, declare the six rows in 12.2 with their placeholders and in 12.8 with their fakes, and ask the plan owner to add the C rows of P5, P6, P1, P3 and P7 to the key

title: RWB-S6-E6006: the legacy endpoint row and R-DS-23 name the award, while API-S6-003 and R-DS-19 are RWB-S6-E6005-APP's and LotAwarded is attributed to that story
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; Work Package B2-S6-009 story lines RWB-S6-E6006-APP and RWB-S6-E6006-CON; legacy RWB-E6-006 Endpoints, Permission checks and AC2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-19, R-DS-23 and R-DS-24; TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T4, T5.3 and Appendix T-A.1; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.9 and A2.10; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 43
description: (1) R-DS-23 is one sentence with two halves, 'Award the lot' and 'generate the sale agreement and the customer notices', and the split plan puts its criterion in RWB-S6-E6006-APP while the award operation POST /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award, the price test R-DS-19 and the buyer columns are the award story's, so the two stories must not both claim the award. (2) The legacy Endpoints table of RWB-E6-006 rows API-S6-003, which the target builds under RWB-S6-E6005-APP, so this story provides no operation of its own and the legacy A right of RW-DEBTSALE, RW-PRODHEAD and RW-HEADASL is exercised there, not here. (3) Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives the service LotAwarded, which the sibling stories attribute to RWB-S6-E6005-APP, so this step publishes nothing and the award fact reaches rwb-case on the case-move answer and other consumers on the lot read. (4) The FSD gives the feature no primary role at all ('None; runs unattended') while the legacy permission table gives three roles the A right, so the authority of the step is stated as the service identity plus the read right.
evidence: legacy RWB-E6-006 Endpoints row POST /api/recovery/v1/debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award, Permission checks row Debt sale A with RW-DEBTSALE, RW-PRODHEAD and RW-HEADASL, and AC2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-19 (AWARD_PENDING) and R-DS-23 (AWARD_CONFIRMED, LOT_AWARDED); TSD S6 T-A.1 API-S6-003; FSD S6 A2.10.3.3 'None; runs unattended | Primary'; Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT and slide 43 row 23 (LotAwarded consumers rwb-case and rwb-payment)
area: Story boundary, operation disposition and event attribution
proposed: Read R-DS-23 as the award effect only, keep the price test, API-S6-003 and the buyer columns with RWB-S6-E6005-APP, declare no provided operation and no event in this story, and record the disposition in the traceability of both stories

title: RWB-S6-E6006: the lot has no column for the agreement or the notice references, no source states the lot status at award, and no requirement row names the agreement or the notices
source: Template and Rules v1 R7.3 and R9; TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T8; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.10, requirements served and the field catalog of A2.10; legacy RWB-E6-006 Data table and Screen and states; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DS-23
description: (1) debt_sale_lot carries DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-030 and nothing that holds the reference of the sale agreement or of the customer notices, and document and notice are P5's and P6's tables, so the two references live in the decision record and in the custody of their owners and nowhere in this schema. (2) LOV-LOT-STATUS is BUILDING, OFFERED, AWARDED, TRANSFERRED and CLOSED, and no source states that the award step changes the lot status, so the write of AWARDED is declared here instead of inferred. (3) No FSD requirement row names the agreement or the notices: REQ-S6-006 covers the award and its recorded price, TSD S6 T8 maps the FEAT-DBS rows to REQ-S6-001 to REQ-S6-009 without a row for FEAT-DBS-10, and the split plan carries no requirement id for the slice, so REQ-S6-006 is traced as the nearest row. (4) The legacy Screen and states table gives SCR-26 the states Open, closed, awarded and transferred and no source maps them to the lot status and the case route state together.
evidence: TSD S6 T3.1 debt_sale_lot fields DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-030 and debt_sale_account DF-SAL-031 to DF-SAL-037; TSD S6 T3.2 LOV-LOT-STATUS; TSD S6 T8 rows REQ-S6-001 to REQ-S6-009 with no FEAT-DBS-10 row; FSD S6 requirements served REQ-S6-006 Must E6; legacy RWB-E6-006 Data table and Screen and states 'SCR-26 Award | Open; closed; awarded; transferred'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-23
area: Data model of the references, lot status and requirement mapping
proposed: Hold the two references in the decision record and in the custody of rwb-document and rwb-comms, declare the write of AWARDED on the lot status, trace REQ-S6-006 as the nearest requirement and ask for a requirement row and, if the business needs it, a reference column in a later DB change

title: RWB-S6-E6006: the addressee of the notices is the ACE customer view v_ace_customer, and no source gives the notice types, the templates or the masking rule of the letter
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R9; legacy RWB-E6-006 Data table (v_ace_customer, notice) and AC1; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.10.2 and A2.10.3.1; TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T3.1, T5.1, T6.1 and T6.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 29, 37, 41 and 45; Feature List v4 rows FEAT-OCC-01, FEAT-OCC-02 and FEAT-OCC-05
description: (1) The legacy data table reads the customer from v_ace_customer with DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074, and in the target the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views are read by rwb-source-data alone, so the addressee of a notice must arrive on that owner's contract with its as-of date and the plan's pattern set carries DP-05 without a C row. (2) A customer notice must name its addressee, while the platform rule forbids personal data in events, workflow inputs and logs and this service may hold no PII: no source states how the addressee travels to rwb-comms, so it is passed inside the notice request only and kept in no column, record or log. (3) No source gives the notice types, the notice and agreement templates, their versions or the masking and conduct rules that apply to a sale notice, so all of them are read as reference data and package values of rwb-comms, rwb-document and rwb-decision with the placeholder. (4) The FSD names the PII service as an integration point of the module and no contract for it exists in the target.
evidence: legacy RWB-E6-006 Data table rows v_ace_customer DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074 and notice DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023; FSD S6 A2.10.2 'Integration points. Workbench, WIN' and A2.2.2 'PII service'; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 37 ('only rwb-source-data has SELECT on the views') and slide 45; TSD S6 T6.2 (masking applies to personal fields); Feature List v4 rows FEAT-OCC-01 (letter from an approved template), FEAT-OCC-02 (dispatch through WIN) and FEAT-OCC-05 (conduct check before every outbound contact)
area: Personal data, reference data and notice content
proposed: Read the addressee on the rwb-source-data contract, pass it inside the notice request only, read the notice types and templates as versioned reference data of rwb-comms and rwb-document, and record the placeholder until those owners publish them

title: RWB-S6-E6006: the FSD names WIN as an integration point and FEAT-OCC-07 as the prerequisite, and neither is a row of the C, I or X set of this story
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R9; legacy RWB-E6-006 Depends on FEAT-OCC-07; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A2.10.2 and A1.2; TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T5.1; Feature List v4 rows FEAT-OCC-02 and FEAT-OCC-07; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 8 (WIN, daily letters file INT-14) and slide 41 P2 and P6
section: Metadata (External dependencies, Integration dependencies); Sections 2, 3, 4, 12.2, 12.9, 13 and 19
description: (1) The legacy story and the FSD name WIN as an integration point of the feature and the legacy Depends on row names FEAT-OCC-07, which the Feature List places in P6 Communications as the template-driven generation of contract and approval documents. (2) In the target WIN is the daily letters file INT-14 outside the cluster, reached by rwb-comms for the despatch and by rwb-integration for the file, and the platform rules give the X class to outside systems: the plan's X row is None and no C row carries P2 or the P6 despatch, so neither the file nor the WIN channel has a build row of this story. (3) FEAT-OCC-07 is not a feature of S6 and does not appear in the FSD A1.2 feature list of the module, so the prerequisite is read as the P5 document generation and the P6 templates rather than as a call from the debt sale step.
evidence: legacy RWB-E6-006 Depends on FEAT-OCC-07; FSD S6 A2.10.2 'Integration points. Workbench, WIN'; TSD S6 T5.1 row INT-25 only; Feature List v4 row FEAT-OCC-02 ('Dispatch a letter through WIN and capture proof of delivery', P6) and row FEAT-OCC-07 ('Generate contract, credit approval and mortgage documents', P6); Architecture v5 slide 8 'WIN daily letters file (INT-14)'; Work Package B2-S6-009 story line with X empty
proposed: Keep the X and I rows as the plan states them, read the WIN despatch as rwb-comms's and the INT-14 file as rwb-comms's and rwb-integration's in 12.9, and ask the plan owner to record the P6 and P2 rows the notice channel needs

title: RWB-S6-E6006: EP06 puts the story in wave 4 and release 30 April 2027 while rwb-debtsale is an Arch v5 wave 3 service
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 (W-MAP), R5.7 and R9; Work Package B2-S6-009 story line RWB-S6-E6006-APP; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 42; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 A1.2 (FEAT-DBS-10 first in E6); legacy RWB-E6-006 (Epic row E6, release 30 April 2027)
section: Metadata (Wave, Release, Business epic); Sections 2, 3 and 18
description: RWB-E6-006 belongs to business epic EP06, whose W-MAP wave is 4, while Architecture v5 gives rwb-debtsale wave 3 and the platform service table of the rules gives S6 wave 3. Rule R5.6 keeps the W-MAP wave only when it is earlier than the service wave, and here it is later, so the story is stated in wave 4 with release 30 April 2027 as the plan gives it, and one service delivers in two waves with two releases. The date is copied unchanged and marked tentative by rule U7 and is not raised as a gap; this row is the S6 and EP06 instance of the conflict the rule asks for, and it repeats the instance already raised by WP B-S6-01 for the same service and epic because each work package writes its own candidates.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 S6 rwb-debtsale wave 3 and slide 42 note (Epics 4-5: S1, S3, S4, S6); Template and Rules R4 service table S6 wave 3 and R5.6 W-MAP EP06 wave 4; Work Package B2-S6-009 story line wave 4 and release 30 April 2027; legacy RWB-E6-006 Epic row 'E6, release 30 April 2027'
proposed: Keep wave 4 and the 30 April 2027 release as the plan and the legacy epic give them, build against the CON baseline in the wave 3 service on Day 1, and state once in the wave map that rwb-debtsale delivers its EP05 keys in wave 3 and its EP06 keys in wave 4

title: RWB-S6-E6006: the extract folder holds no FSD or TSD file whose name contains S6, so the module documents stand in for the extract
source: Template and Rules v1 R7.3 and R9; Work Package B2-S6-009 read list ('_work/msr/extract/ files of the FSD and TSD folders whose name contains S6'); _work/msr/extract listing; FSD S6 Debt sale v3 and TSD S6 Debt sale v2 in the extract folders of the module pair; legacy RWB-E6-006
description: The Work Package asks for the extract files of the FSD and TSD folders whose name contains S6. The run folder holds the module pair one level down, as Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 under Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6 and Recovery Workbench TSD S6 Debt sale v2 under Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, and no flat S6 extract exists at the top of _work/msr/extract. The two module files are the documents an extract would have carried, so they are read directly, the fill order of R7.3 is unchanged and no value is taken from a summary or a slide deck.
evidence: _work/msr/extract listing: the flat folder carries the Program, Epic 1, Epic 2, Epics 3 to 8, Business Rules and Routing Logic, Architecture v5, Temporal and Drools, Event and Messaging, Batch and Scheduling, LDM, NFS, ADR, Decision Log and API Specification extracts, and the S6 pair sits in the sub-folders Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6 and Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5
area: Source availability and rule of fill
proposed: Read FSD S6 v3 and TSD S6 v2 from the module folders for every S6 story, cite them as the module files, and add a flat S6 extract to the extract set before the baseline is tagged
